themes_detail.label: Sudden Panhandling Surge
themes_detail.summary: Panhandling complaints spiked to 7 THIS WEEK, up 331% from the 1.6 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, suggesting a sudden shift in street conditions or enforcement patterns in Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights that warrants investigation into root causes and public safety perception.
evidence: 7 panhandling complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly average (z-score: 5.42)
331% increase in one week suggests rapid emergence rather than gradual trend
High statistical significance (z-score 5.42) indicates anomaly unlikely due to random variation
reporting_angles: Interview business owners, residents, and NYPD to understand what changed this week
Cross-check with local homeless services to see if new encampments or outreach events occurred

themes_detail.label: Street Lights Failing Across District
themes_detail.summary: Street light condition complaints reached 23 THIS WEEK, up 152% from the 9.1 weekly average, indicating a rapid deterioration in public infrastructure and nighttime safety across Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights that requires immediate DOE/Department of Parks response.
evidence: 23 street light complaints THIS WEEK vs. 9.1 weekly average (z-score: 4.54)
152% spike suggests either a weather event, maintenance gap, or equipment failure affecting multiple blocks
Community board has standing request for 'new equipment for maintenance' (Department of Parks)—suggests chronic underinvestment
reporting_angles: Request DOE/Department of Parks data on which blocks are dark, maintenance schedules, and repair backlogs
Photograph dark intersections and interview residents about safety concerns after dark

themes_detail.label: Tree Emergency in Fort Greene
themes_detail.summary: Over the past 3 weeks, two tree-related spikes converged: illegal tree damage complaints (12, up 540% from 1.9 avg) 3 weeks ago and dead/dying trees (9, up 454% from 1.6 avg) 2 weeks ago, alongside this week's overgrown branch complaints (7, up 367%), suggesting active tree damage or deferred maintenance affecting neighborhood canopy and public safety.
evidence: Illegal tree damage: 12 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.9 weekly average (z-score: 5.99, up 540%)
Dead/dying trees: 9 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.6 weekly average (z-score: 6.64, up 454%)
Overgrown tree/branches: 7 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average (z-score: 4.92, up 367%)
Community board has standing request for 'new equipment for maintenance' (Department of Parks)—chronic underfunding
reporting_angles: Investigate whether a single development or contractor damaged multiple trees illegally
Document tree health across Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights parks and streets; interview residents about safety hazards from overgrown branches
Examine Parks Department budget and staffing for tree pruning/removal and whether maintenance has been deferred

themes_detail.label: Residential Appliance Failures
themes_detail.summary: Appliance complaints jumped to 6 THIS WEEK, doubling the 2.0 weekly average (up 200%), suggesting a potential spike in broken heating systems, water heaters, or other essential appliances during early winter that could cascade into heat/hot water complaints (already 803 over 90 days).
evidence: 6 appliance complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.0 weekly average (z-score: 4.62, up 200%)
Heat/hot water already represents 803 complaints over 90 days—seasonal trend likely to worsen
Timing (early winter) suggests heating system failures entering peak season
reporting_angles: Survey tenants about heating/hot water outages and landlord responsiveness
Cross-check HPD violation data for habitability complaints and heat violation trends

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Spike
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints exploded to 4 LAST WEEK, up 3100% from the 0.1 weekly average, the highest z-score anomaly in the dataset (11.72), indicating a sudden, dramatic shift in park use patterns or events in Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights requiring immediate investigation.
evidence: 4 park noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 11.72—highest anomaly in data)
3100% increase is largest percentage spike across all complaint categories
Extremely rare baseline (0.1 avg) means even small absolute numbers represent extraordinary deviation
reporting_angles: Identify which park(s) generated complaints—Fort Greene Park vs. others in district
Investigate whether construction, an event, festival, or new use pattern triggered complaints
Interview Parks Department about recent activity or permits issued
